title: Niacinamide, under the microscope

scenes.text: This is what niacinamide actually does inside your skin.
Deep down, cells called melanocytes make melanin. That's your skin's pigment.
They hand it up to the cells above. Too much of it, and you get a dark spot.
Niacinamide steps in, and slows down that handoff.
Less pigment reaches the surface, so the spot slowly fades.
Bonus: it helps your skin make more ceramides, so your barrier gets stronger.
Two to five percent is enough. Give it eight weeks. Next episode: centella.
